body:
Update:
I tested the nodejs signaling server setup from the editor and a web build as well and I found that I get a lobby id in the nodejs terminal logs and using it I can connect to the server from the editor or the browser instance, but still getting the parsing error and on the godot side of things I cannot see wether I'm connected or not. This is the nodejs log:

`Peer 2127281735 created lobby VX1OY2e4l2HH6yV2
Open lobbies: 1
Peer 2127281735 joining lobby VX1OY2e4l2HH6yV2 with 0 peers
Peer 1011964112 joining lobby VX1OY2e4l2HH6yV2 with 1 peers
Peer 316073570 joining lobby VX1OY2e4l2HH6yV2 with 2 peers
Peer 1083033869 joining lobby VX1OY2e4l2HH6yV2 with 3 peers`

In Godot I can't see any of this in the intended UI and I get the parsing error in the Godot logs.

You got me really worried here!  However, my WebRTC thing still seemed to work https://github.com/goatchurchprime/godot_multiplayer_networking_workbench

Thanks to heavy use of the debugger on that webrtc_signalling demo, the problem can be stated as follows:

* **Godot 4.3:**  `JSON.parse_string('{"id":10}') ->{ "id": 10 }
* **Godot 4.4:**  `JSON.parse_string('{"id":10}') ->{ "id": 10.0 }

The latter then falls foul of the condition: `str(msg.type).is_valid_int()` in the `ws_webrtc.client._parse_msg()` function.

_Numbers_ vs _Integers_ and _Floats_ are an issue in JSON.  You wouldn't have thought the world could mess up something so fundamental as this, but it has, and there are now many different incompatible implementations depending on what language you are using.  The Godot position was elaborated here:  https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/61464 in 2022, though I'm not sure why it fell out of the code until now.  

Probably the most easiest fix is to change the two places where it encodes the numbers to read:
 
```GDScript
return ws.send_text(JSON.stringify({
			"type": str(type),
			"id": str(id),
			"data": data,
		}))
```

So this ticket actually applies to the Godot-Demo-Projects repository.

Coincidentally I just hit a bug in a completely different project caused by this change: 

An id-value was read from a JSON file as `id=3.0` instead of `id=3`.  When a Node was created and named after this number, it got the name `3_0` instead of `3` (since the '.' was converted to an '_').  Then when the Node's name was converted back to an integer by `int(Node.name)` the answer was now 30, which didn't match up with the `3` that was expected.

@goatchurchprime thank you for looking into this so quickly, this got me worried as well as I have a project that I'd like to upgrade for several reasons! But this seems like a trivial workaround, then. Your finding is intriuging as well regarding the number conversions.

Edit: I also tested your workaround, and it works in the non-node version, so thanks again! I guess it needs to be updated in the nodejs code as well, then it should fly again.

I think what we're going to have to do for now is if you want some number to be an integer, cast it using int() after parsing, or change the serialization to use a string (this also avoids the issue where some large integer values are serialized incorrectly).

This really needs to be added to the Godot documentation.

If you want proper integer serialization and parsing (without serializing some int64 values incorrectly), my view is it should be done by implementing my proposal godotengine/godot-proposals#8830

As frustrated as I am that discussion on this as a compatibility issue didn't occur until the second release candidate was already out, I do not personally think 4.4 release should be delayed over this issue, given that the workaround in projects is not too complicated.

Furthermore, the old behavior was very subtly wrong in a misleading way: in 4.3 and earlier, it was not a given that values would be properly converted to integer. This way, the behavior is always consistent (or consistently wrong if you want integers), and you can always solve it with an int cast. In engineering terms, this is preferable over the old status quo where some floats would be parsed as integers depending on how they were serialized.

If you think the compromise that documenting all JSON numbers to be floats (and recommend to cast to int() or serialize as string) and is not good enough, and that this should be a release blocker, we need to come up with a pragmatic approach to address this problem that can be done without delaying 4.4 significantly for everyone.

> @lyuma: As frustrated as I am that discussion on this as a compatibility issue didn't occur until the second release candidate was already out,

I have had proposal https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/11277 open for awhile, which discusses adding a function for the pre-4.4 behavior of stringifying floats, and possibly changing `String::num` to the old behavior. It requires core devs feedback.

I want the parse_string() function to behave like it did in version 4.3. Since I upgraded to version 4.4, it has broken all my ID values.
Parse_string() has been changed for good reason - it was hiding LOTS of bugs in user scripts, and making people believe JSON supported both ints and floats
but JSON has numbers right? which is not int or float as it can present as any of those
